text:
Hannah (sales): Hi all — Quick escalation from the Vega POC: customer sees logs in Splunk but traces don't stitch. They only have a request_id field. Need a short triage and workaround we can hand to their SREs.
Luca (infra): Likely causes: (1) intermediary dropping non-standard headers (WAF/nginx/sidecar), (2) forwarder transform remapping headers incorrectly, or (3) spans dropped during HEC rate limiting (HTTP 429). Any headers client is sending?
Mei (support): They send both `traceparent` and `x-vega-trace`. ALB access logs include them, but the Splunk events indexed by the forwarder do not. We also saw some forwarder 429s last night.
Luca (infra): Ok. Fast checklist for SREs: 1) curl the header-echo endpoint to confirm header reaches the app; 2) check ingress access_log for the header; 3) inspect forwarder transforms for remapping/synthesis; 4) check forwarder logs for 429s.
Hannah (sales): Customer cannot change WAF rules during business hours. They requested a POC-safe workaround that requires minimal infra changes.
Luca (infra): Two POC-safe options: A) use a WAF-allowed header like `x-request-id` and map it to `trace_id` in the forwarder; B) if changing client header is impossible, add a forwarder transform that synthesizes `trace_id` from `request_id` when trace headers are absent. Option A preserves propagated context; B is a pragmatic fallback for dashboards.
Mei (support): Can you paste example remap/synth snippets I can hand over?
Luca (infra): Sure — Vector remap pseudo-config to prefer propagated trace then fall back to x-request-id:

  transforms.remap.type = "remap"
  transforms.remap.source = '''
    .trace_id = if exists(.headers["x-vega-trace"]) { .headers["x-vega-trace"] }
               else if exists(.headers["x-request-id"]) { .headers["x-request-id"] }
               else null
  '''

And a tiny Lua synth fallback in FluentD/Vector pipeline:

  function process(event)
    if not event.trace_id and event.request_id then
      event.trace_id = event.request_id
    end
    return event
  end

Mei (support): Great. Any caveats we should warn the customer/SOC about?
Luca (infra): Yes: synthesized trace_ids let you join logs and spans for dashboards, but they do not reconstruct parent-child relationships across services. Note that synthesizing does not introduce new PII — request_id is already present in logs and redaction rules still apply. Also call out that retries/buffering to avoid 429s can cause duplicates; for POC duplicates are usually acceptable.
Hannah (sales): They also asked whether missing trace headers could break KV cache usage in SDKs and affect inference performance.
Luca (infra): If the SDK uses trace_id as a KV cache key and span events are dropped or keys are missing, you might see cache misses which increase latency and token cost. This is why avoid drops (fix 429s) — buffering + retries or increasing HEC quota are important.
Mei (support): We saw forwarder logs with 429s: snippet: `2026-03-20T23:15:07Z forwarder WARN http 429 hec.vega.com rate_limit avg=9/min`. That aligns with the time ranges where traces weren't stitched.
Luca (infra): Parallel action plan: (1) implement remap/synth in forwarder as immediate fallback, (2) increase forwarder buffer (FORWARDER_BUFFER_BYTES=100MB) and retries (FORWARDER_RETRIES=5), (3) open support ticket with Splunk to request temporary HEC rate bump for POC if spikes continue.
Hannah (sales): Can we give them a simple smoke test to validate success after changes?
Luca (infra): Yes — two-step smoke test: (A) header echo: `curl -H "x-vega-trace: poc-VE-01" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/debug/header-echo` -> server should echo header in response JSON; (B) Splunk search: `index=vega trace_id="poc-VE-01" | head 10` should return within 60s. Add CI assertion to hit the debug endpoint and search the index as acceptance criteria for POC.
Mei (support): Customer also wants a short SOC/GDPR-friendly statement to include in their security questionnaire. Draft suggestion?
Luca (infra): Draft for SOC: "By default our ingest pipeline applies redaction rules to remove common PII fields; trace headers used for correlation (e.g., traceparent/x-vega-trace) are preserved end-to-end unless an intermediary explicitly rewrites or drops them. For POCs, we provide a playbook to recover correlation via forwarder remapping or synthesis; synthesis is used only as a fallback and does not introduce additional PII."
Hannah (sales): Perfect. Any automation we can add to prevent this in future POCs?
Luca (infra): Yes — add a CI smoke into onboarding that: hits header-echo, asserts header in Splunk index, and a monitoring rule: `forwarder_429_rate > 5/min for 5m -> page infra`. Also include a deployment check that ensures proxy/nginx configs have `proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent;` style passthroughs.

Mei (support): Customer accepted the remap fallback and will schedule a WAF rule change in a maintenance window. They deployed the Vector remap and increased buffer.

Hannah (sales): Customer reports trace_id now appears in Splunk and dashboards stitch. They're happy with the wording for SOC. Closing — thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
